explicit_interfaces: Compactness, convexity and positive definiteness of K
Brouwer fixed points for continuous K self-maps
Crossing sets depend only on threshold graphs
The packing predicate is monotone and closed in K times R
The literal maximal-packing obstruction and original r-tree crossing bound
The quantified simultaneous-response property, discharged in the application by the hierarchy proof
not_assumed: Existence of a continuous interpolating response map
The desired nearly preserved tree packing

hypotheses: H is a finite indexed loopless undirected multigraph on at least two vertices
H contains r edge-disjoint spanning trees
K is a nonempty compact convex set of real symmetric positive definite matrices
The simultaneous response property holds with the displayed quantifier order and all original crossing edges
threshold.response_quantifiers: forall X in K, exists Y in K, forall s>0
threshold.crossing_edges: All original H edges crossing the maximal packing partition, including edges absent from the threshold graph.

application.cutoff: Absolute and sufficiently large to satisfy q>=q_H, q>=r/2, r>=2^31 and 40*r^(-3/16)<1.

exact_sample.classification: Finite arithmetic regression, not a proof of the universal theorem

negative_control.claim: Inversion does not commute with convex averaging; this is not an assertion made by the manuscript.

jacobian.classification: One bounded exact inverse sanity calculation; not evidence for a universal threshold conclusion.

external_inputs: Anari--Oveis Gharan, arXiv:1411.4613v4, Section 3.1 definition and Theorem 3.5
